correctness.rationale: The polynomial identity R_n(u)=sum_{j=0}^n (n!/j!)u^j gives recurrence R_n=nR_(n-1)+u^n. All but the last term of R_m have factor m, hence R_(n+m)=u^m R_n mod m by induction. The lcm(m,ord_m(u)) is a period. Any period P yields P=u(1-u^P) and P(1+u)=u^2(1-u^P) modulo m from the n=1,2 recurrence comparisons, forcing 1-u^P=0 and P=0 mod m when u is a unit. These are full necessity and sufficiency. Finite abelian group exponent structure proves all divisor-order spectra. verify.py independently checked all 773 unit pairs for m=2..50 and their proper divisors, 49 complete spectra, and 56 permutation identities.

value.rationale: The object is the natural rencontres fixed-point weighted permutation enumerator; modular least periods and the set of all periods obtainable by varying the weight are canonical arithmetic invariants, especially over composite moduli. The result classifies every invertible weight and arbitrary m>=2, rules out all shorter periods, identifies all realizable periods m*d via Carmichael exponent, and supplies sharp extremal periods and their count. This is a complete motivated two-parameter classification, not a preselected numerical improvement or textbook restatement of an already explicit period formula. It has a short self-contained proof and leaves nonunit weights untouched.
